reasons: Classification is correct: the only indemnity (Article XII) runs solely against Licensee, and Article XIII expressly negates any Licensor liability for third-party infringement claims — that is walk-away territory under INDEMN and clearly fails the fallback (no Vendor IP indemnity), so a deviation finding with a redline is warranted, not over-flagging.

The inserted Article XII-A tracks the preferred position and model language: IP infringement, breach of law, Licensor-caused data incidents, gross negligence/wilful misconduct, plus notice/control/cooperation mechanics; it also expressly overrides Article XIII's limitations and infringement carve-out, which is necessary or the new indemnity would be illusory.

Narrowing of Licensee's indemnity (dropping 'sole responsibility' for exercising the licence and 'conduct of Licensee's business' in favour of Licensee-provided content and Licensee's breach of law) is exactly what the rule's redline guidance directs for one-sided clauses, so the high changed-character ratio on p0128 is justified rather than excessive; the retained breach-of-agreement prong is a minor residual, not a defect.

Comment is accurate, concise, uses the required prefix and first person plural, explains the Article XIII conflict, and offers the fallback (usual IP exclusions/remedies plus 3x annual fees super-cap).
Severity 'critical' is appropriate given absence of any Vendor IP indemnity combined with an express infringement liability disclaimer.
